# Little Bigtable vs Google Cloud Bigtable Emulator

**Little Bigtable lets developers keep a reusable Bigtable environment and test
more of an application's lifecycle locally:** resource setup, backup/restore,
change-stream consumption, restricted views and SQL queries, alongside normal
row operations.

Google's emulator is a convenient in-memory choice for basic local Bigtable
tests. Little Bigtable adds persistent SQLite/PostgreSQL storage and broader
local API behavior. Both are development emulators; neither replaces the
managed service for production qualification.

## Baselines and evidence

Comparison reviewed **2026-10-20**:

| Baseline | Identity and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Google Cloud SDK emulator | Google's [emulator guide][G1], checked 2026-10-20. It explicitly documents volatile storage, no instance/cluster management and no secure connection. No packaged Cloud SDK binary was tested for this comparison. |
| Google open-source implementation | `googleapis/google-cloud-go` commit [`3266de7c69fd3c05c921823bcfd92b0a8f0b1ffa`][G0], fetched 2026-10-20. All three non-test Go files in `bigtable/bttest` were inspected: `inmem.go`, `instance_server.go`, `validation.go`. The [`cbtemulator` entry point][G8] uses that package. This source snapshot is not proof of the version bundled in a particular Cloud SDK release. |
| Little Bigtable | v0.5.0, commit `dd5f9e796de1e3700271028f36a80c6a5957705f`, branch `jay-bigtable-extended`; [compatibility audit](BIGTABLE_COMPATIBILITY.md) dated 2026-10-04. The reconciliation checkout `d3ec4c4` adds documentation to that runtime baseline. |

`cbt` is the [client CLI][G9], not the emulator server. This comparison targets
the Cloud SDK Bigtable emulator and its inspected upstream implementation.
It also differs from comparing our branch with the original Little Bigtable
`master`, which already had SQLite persistence.

In the table, **documented** refers to Google's guide; **source** refers to the
pinned open-source implementation. **No handler** means there is no concrete
implementation in that package, including methods inherited through its embedded
server interfaces. It does not assert a tested gRPC status for an unrun binary.
Fork evidence names existing behavioral tests; the full contract and historical
results remain in the audit. An implemented API can still be locally simplified.

## Side-by-side features

This table summarizes developer value. For individual checkmarks and counts,
see the [detailed feature scorecard](#detailed-feature-scorecard).

| Capability | Google emulator: documented or inspected source | Little Bigtable v0.5.0 | Developer benefit | Fork evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Persistent environments | **Documented:** memory only; state lost between runs. [G1][G1] | SQLite or PostgreSQL; row and admin state retained in the database. | Reuse fixtures and test restarts without rebuilding the environment. | [Storage conformance](bttest/storage_conformance_test.go): `TestStorageConformance` |
| Instance and cluster lifecycle | **Documented:** no management APIs. **Source:** create/get/list/update stubs. [G1][G1], [G2][G2] | Persistent metadata CRUD, validation, guarded deletion; capacity remains metadata. | Exercise bootstrap and teardown code locally. | [Instance admin](bttest/instance_admin_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceInstanceAdminOfficialClient` |
| App profiles | **Source:** CRUD stubs. [G2][G2] | Persistent profiles; routing validation for transactions and streams. | Catch invalid routing configuration during development. | [Instance admin](bttest/instance_admin_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceInstanceAdminAppProfileRouting`; [targets](bttest/targets_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceTargetAppProfileResolution` |
| Basic rows and tables | **Documented:** table creation and row reads/writes. [G1][G1] | Reads, mutations, families and ranges, with explicit local contracts. | Keep standard SDK workflows while adding lifecycle coverage. | [Go-client workflow](bttest/google_docs_hello_test.go): `TestGoogleDocsHelloWorldGoClientWorkflow` |
| Deletion protection and recovery | **Source:** protection already implemented; hard delete; no undelete handler. [G3][G3] | Protection persists; soft delete and undelete within seven days. | Test protection across restarts and recovery after deletion. | [Table admin](bttest/table_admin_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceTableAdminUpdateTablePersistsAcrossRestart`, `TestConformanceTableAdminDeleteUndelete` |
| Backups, copies and restore | **Source:** no handlers. [G0][G0] | Immutable schema/row snapshots, copy and restore independent of the source. | Test recovery after source changes, deletion and restart. | [Backups](bttest/backup_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceBackupRestoreAfterSourceDeletedAndRestart`, `TestConformanceBackupCopyRules` |
| Change streams | **Source:** no streaming RPC handlers. [G0][G0] | Opt-in persistent records, retention, tokens and heartbeats; one partition. | Develop consumers and checkpoint/resume logic locally. | [Change streams](bttest/change_stream_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceChangeStreamResumeWithContinuationToken`, `TestConformanceChangeStreamHeartbeats` |
| Authorized views | **Source:** CRUD explicitly `Unimplemented`. [G4][G4] | Persistent CRUD and subset enforcement for rows, families and qualifiers. | Check restricted data paths and rejected out-of-view writes. | [Authorized views](bttest/authorized_view_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceAuthorizedViewReadRestriction`, `TestConformanceAuthorizedViewWriteRestriction` |
| GoogleSQL queries | **Source:** `PrepareQuery`/`ExecuteQuery` explicitly `Unimplemented`. [G5][G5] | Local parsing, type checks, parameters and execution; SQL subset. | Exercise query code through the official Go client. | [Queries](bttest/query_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceSQLQueryThroughClient` |
| Logical views | **Source:** no handlers. [G0][G0] | Persistent, validated definitions queryable through SQL. | Test reusable application query definitions. | [Queries](bttest/query_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceLogicalViewQuery` |
| Continuous materialized views | **Source:** no CRUD handlers. [G0][G0] | GoogleSQL definitions, restart persistence, read-only results refreshed before reads. | Test derived aggregates and secondary-index query shapes locally. | [Queries](bttest/query_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceMaterializedViewReadsAndRefresh`, `TestConformanceMaterializedViewSurvivesRestart`; [CMV reference](CMV_SUPPORT.md) |
| Schema bundles | **Source:** no handlers. [G0][G0] | Proto/Avro validation, CRUD, limits and etags. | Exercise schema registration and compatibility checks. | [Schema bundles](bttest/schema_bundle_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceSchemaBundleProtoCRUD`, `TestConformanceSchemaBundleAvroCRUD` |
| IAM policy workflows | **Source:** policy RPC stubs. [G2][G2] | Persistent policies, etags and masks; **no identity enforcement**. | Let configuration code exercise policy lifecycle, not access security. | [IAM](bttest/iam_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceIAMPersistsAcrossRestart`, `TestConformanceIAMEtagAborted` |
| Long-running operations | **Source:** returns completed table-update operations; no Operations service registration. [G3][G3] | Durable Get/List/Wait/Delete/Cancel registry; no cloud provisioning delay. | Test operation polling and persisted operation handles. | [Operations](bttest/operations_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceOperationsDurableAcrossRestart`, `TestConformanceOperationsWaitDeleteCancel` |
| Session protocol | **Source:** configuration and Open* RPCs explicitly `Unimplemented`. [G5][G5] | Sessions share local read/write validation and view restrictions. | Exercise session errors, read-only mode and view targets. | [Sessions](bttest/session_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceSessionPermissionsAndErrors`, `TestConformanceSessionAuthorizedViewRestrictions` |
| Aggregate mutations | **Source:** Add/Merge and Int64 sum already present. [G6][G6] | Typed Sum/Min/Max Int64 and HLL++; local sketch format. | Test additional aggregate-family behavior. | [Writes](bttest/data_write_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceWriteAggregateSemantics`, `TestConformanceWriteAggregateFamilyTypeChecks` |
| Advanced filters | **Source:** many standard filters; no Sink/ValueBitmask cases; unknown cell filters can pass through. [G7][G7] | All pinned RowFilter variants, including Sink/ValueBitmask, validated before reads. | Catch invalid filter requests and exercise those missing variants. | [Filters](bttest/filter_conformance_test.go): `TestConformanceFilterSinkDocExample`, `TestConformanceFilterValueBitmask`, `TestConformanceFilterValidationBeforeRead` |
| SDK/CLI qualification | **Documented:** client-library support. [G1][G1] | Official Go client and core pinned `cbt` smoke; other languages unverified. | Review exactly which local client workflows are covered. | [CLI conformance](bttest/client_conformance_test.go): `TestCBTClientConformance` |

## Detailed feature scorecard

Each row below names **one RPC, field, filter, mutation, storage entity, SQL
function or observable behavior**. Headings organize the rows; they do not
combine multiple methods into a single checkmark. The high-level table above
provides the developer benefits; this scorecard provides the detailed inventory.

Jump to [RPCs](#every-registered-rpc), [request fields](#every-pinned-requestschema-field),
[filters](#every-rowfilter-variant), [GC](#every-gc-rule-variant),
[mutations](#every-mutation-field), [persistence](#every-persisted-sql-entity),
[behavior details](#additional-behaviors-and-explicit-boundaries), or
[SQL functions](#every-inventoried-sql-function-and-syntax-form).

### Legend and counting rules

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ✓ | Implements the stated local capability. This is not a claim of complete production semantics or every overload. |
| ◐ | Useful local behavior with a material simplification or incomplete contract; the row or audit explains the limit. |
| ✗ | Capability absent, ignored, explicitly rejected or outside the emulator's local scope. It does not imply a particular gRPC status for an unrun binary. |
| ? | Not established by the available evidence; excluded from supported counts. |
| — | Not applicable to that column. |

The Google column is **source-inspected at the pinned commit**, not a new test
of a packaged Cloud SDK release. Fork RPC/field marks follow the executable
ledger (`supported` → ✓, `locally_simplified` → ◐, unsupported/not-applicable → ✗).
Other rows name the narrower operation being compared and cite source or tests.
Upstream partial RPC marks describe the specific limits in that row; there is
no upstream executable ledger equivalent used here.

Counts are **inventory counts, not performance benchmarks or a production-parity
percentage**. The RPC denominator is all 89 registered fork RPCs, including
intentional unsupported responses. Field coverage is all 42 ledger fields in
eight pinned messages; it is not every nested field in all Bigtable protos.
SQL coverage is the union of the checked-in reference-name inventory, public
runtime registry names and four syntax forms; aliases count as distinct names,
not separate overloads. Operators, nested protobuf fields and function overloads
are outside these exhaustive inventories.

### Coverage metrics

Inventory validation on 2026-10-20 compared every detailed row and count with the
compiled ledger, protobuf descriptors, SQL schema and runtime SQL registries.
The existing ledger checks and full local `bttest/internal/gsql` suite passed
with Go 1.27.1 on macOS ARM64. These checks validate the local inventories and
existing local tests; they are not new Google-emulator or production runs.

| Inventory | Rows | Google ✓ | Google ◐ | Google ✗ | Google ? | Fork ✓ | Fork ◐ | Fork ✗ | Fork ? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Registered RPCs | 89 | 2 | 15 | 72 | 0 | 45 | 35 | 9 | 0 |
| Pinned request/schema fields | 42 | 10 | 15 | 17 | 0 | 39 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| RowFilter variants | 20 | 18 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 20 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| GC rule variants | 4 | 3 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Mutation fields (6 variants + timestamp_origin) | 7 | 4 | 2 | 1 | 0 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Read-modify-write operations | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Aggregate family types | 4 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Persisted SQL entities | 15 | 0 | 0 | 15 | 0 | 15 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Additional behaviors and boundaries | 51 | 2 | 0 | 49 | 0 | 30 | 1 | 19 | 1 |
| SQL function/syntax names | 230 | 0 | 0 | 230 | 0 | 203 | 0 | 27 | 0 |

For RPCs, **17/89** upstream methods and **80/89** fork methods provide useful
local behavior (✓ + ◐): **63 additional RPCs** in the fork on this denominator.
The fork retains 5 deprecated snapshot RPCs as unsupported and 4 hardware RPCs
as outside local scope. The SQL inventory contains **203 implemented names and
27 explicitly unsupported names** in the fork; upstream query RPCs are stubs.

Do **not** add inventory totals: a filter can appear as a RowFilter variant,
inside a request field and within ReadRows. The additional-behavior rows also
expand existing RPCs and include explicit non-goals. This preserves visibility
without inflating a single “features supported” number.

## Choosing and demonstrating the value

Choose Google's emulator for disposable row/table tests when its documented
scope meets the application's needs. Choose Little Bigtable when tests need
persistent state or the broader workflows above and can accept the stated local
limits. SQLite avoids an external database; PostgreSQL requires one.

Three useful demonstrations map directly to behavioral tests:

1. **Keep state across restart:** create a table, write data, restart the entire
   emulator harness against the same database and read the data again
   (`TestStorageConformance`).
2. **Recover from a deleted source:** snapshot a table, delete the source,
   restart and restore its original schema and rows
   (`TestConformanceBackupRestoreAfterSourceDeletedAndRestart`).
3. **Test application data boundaries and queries:** read through a restricted
   view, reject an out-of-view write, and prepare/execute a parameterized SQL
   query (`TestConformanceAuthorizedViewWriteRestriction`,
   `TestConformanceSQLQueryThroughClient`).

Use the [build guide's checks](Build_and_Integration.md#run-tests) to reproduce
relevant tests. Test names are traceable evidence, not a claim that the packaged
Google emulator was run through these scenarios.

## Limits and qualification

- **Local behavior:** single process; no replication, failover, real capacity,
  autoscaling, cloud performance or durability guarantees. IAM is permissive;
  authorized-view subset enforcement does not establish identity authorization.
- **Feature limits:** single change-stream partition with watermark/start-time
  caveats; unsupported GoogleSQL functions/types and parameterized logical
  views; emulator-specific HLL++ bytes and multi-column CMV keys. CMV refresh
  timing differs from production. Automated-backup policies do not schedule
  backups. See the audit's [remaining gaps](BIGTABLE_COMPATIBILITY.md#remaining-local-gaps)
  and [CMV limits](CMV_SUPPORT.md#known-limitations).
- **Reconciliation checks (2026-10-20):** selected ledger, SQLite restart,
  backup/restore, authorized-view, query/CMV, IAM persistence, GC and table-update
  persistence tests passed on macOS ARM64 with Go 1.27.1. The revised Go-library
  startup example was also compiled and run. This was a focused check, not a new
  full-suite audit or a PostgreSQL/CLI/platform run.
- **Evidence layers:** the [audit](BIGTABLE_COMPATIBILITY.md#evidence-summary)
  records the historical v0.5.0 full-suite result. The ledger's `test_verified`
  entries include tests of simplified and explicitly unsupported behavior;
  “89 registered RPCs” does not mean 89 fully implemented production RPCs.
  PostgreSQL CI, multi-platform builds, registry publication and LocalCloud
  platform/REST/Console validation are separate evidence layers.
- **Comparison scope:** Google documentation and exact upstream source were
  inspected. No packaged Cloud SDK binary, differential runtime comparison,
  performance benchmark, registry publication or LocalCloud platform run was
  performed for this document. Do not advertise blanket production parity or
  universal client compatibility from this table.

When updating the comparison, refresh both baselines, inspect every affected
handler and retain the supporting test and limitation. Only promote an upstream
source observation to a packaged-emulator runtime claim after recording the
Cloud SDK/emulator version and running that case.
